Confused by Anatomy and Physiology? This complete introduction to A&P overview simplifies the human body's structure, function, homeostasis, and all major organ systems. Perfect for pre-nursing, anaphy nursing year 1, medical students, or anyone starting their biology journey with Organized Biology!

Dive deep into the fascinating world of Human Anatomy and Physiology with this foundational lesson from Organized Biology! We make complex A&P concepts SIMPLE, helping you understand the "big picture" before tackling detailed chapters.
In this video, you'll learn:
1. The core relationship between Anatomy (structure) and Physiology (function).
2. The crucial concept of Homeostasis – how your body maintains a stable internal environment.
3. The levels of organization, from cells to organ systems.
4. How essential nutrients and oxygen are delivered (Digestive, Respiratory, Cardiovascular systems).
5. The communication networks of the body: The Nervous System and Endocrine System.
6. How your body protects itself with the Integumentary, Lymphatic, Immune, Skeletal, and Muscular systems.
7. An introduction to the Reproductive System.
8.How all these systems work together to maintain life!

This lesson is ideal for students in A&P 1, Biology, pre-med, pre-nursing, anaphy 1st year students, or any healthcare field.

description:

📌Watch my Essay Writing Masterclass: https://www.doctorshaene.com/essay-masterclass

When I was a kid, the first thing I associated with a doctor was anatomy. Doctors know about the human body. Simple. It was only when I got to university that I realised that it wasn't quite so simple. Memorising human anatomy was a mammoth visual task. Just memorising the words and knowing what they meant was hard enough. But learning anatomy with just words is ridiculous and inefficient. Instead, I started with visual diagrams and pictures. Then I read the sentences to see if they were a legit description of what I was seeing. Eventually with practice, I could just close my eyes, picture the structures and start describing what I was seeing using my own words.
